rows.label: Julius Caesar
rows.hook: crossed the Rubicon, seized power as dictator, and was stabbed by senators on the Ides of March

rows.label: Augustus
rows.description: first emperor of the Roman Empire and founder of the Julio-Claudian dynasty
rows.hook: became the first emperor after defeating his rivals and ended a long era of civil war

rows.label: Marcus Aurelius
rows.description: 16th Roman Emperor from 161 to 180 and Stoic philosopher
rows.hook: ruled as a philosopher-emperor and wrote the Stoic journal known as the Meditations

rows.label: Nero
rows.description: fifth and last Roman Emperor of Julio-Claudian dynasty (54–68)
rows.hook: is infamous for fiddling while the city burned, and blamed a new religious sect for the fire

rows.label: Caligula
rows.hook: is remembered as a cruel, unstable emperor who reportedly wanted to make his horse a consul

rows.label: Tutankhamun
rows.hook: was a boy king whose almost intact golden tomb was discovered in the Valley of the Kings

rows.label: Constantine the Great
rows.description: Roman emperor from 306 to 337 and first to convert to Christianity (272–337)
rows.hook: legalized Christianity in the empire and moved the capital to a new city on the Bosphorus

rows.label: Seneca
rows.description: Roman Stoic philosopher, statesman and dramatist (c. 4 BCE–65 CE)
rows.hook: was a Stoic philosopher and playwright who tutored a future emperor and was later forced to take his own life

rows.label: Ramesses II
rows.description: Egyptian third pharaoh of the Nineteenth Dynasty
rows.hook: was a long-reigning, monument-building pharaoh who fought the Hittites at Kadesh and built Abu Simbel

rows.label: Cicero
rows.description: Roman statesman, lawyer, orator, and philosopher (106–43 BC)
rows.hook: was a famed orator and lawyer whose speeches against Catiline are still studied

rows.label: Tiberius
rows.description: second Roman Emperor from 14 to 37 AD
rows.hook: succeeded his stepfather as emperor and spent his later years in seclusion on the island of Capri

rows.label: Mark Antony
rows.description: Roman politician and general (83 BC – 30 BC)
rows.hook: was a general who allied with a famous queen of the Nile and lost at the naval battle of Actium

rows.label: Marcus Vipsanius Agrippa
rows.hook: was the first emperor's loyal general who won at Actium and built the Pantheon

rows.label: Commodus
rows.hook: was a gladiator-obsessed emperor and the unworthy son of a philosopher, killed in his bath

rows.label: Sulla
rows.hook: was the first to march his army on the capital, then made himself dictator and posted death lists

rows.label: Claudius
rows.hook: was found hiding behind a curtain after an assassination, was made emperor, and invaded Britain

rows.label: Hadrian
rows.hook: ordered a great defensive wall across northern Britain and rebuilt the Pantheon

rows.label: Pompey
rows.hook: was a great general who shared power in a triumvirate before being defeated by his former son-in-law

rows.label: Trajan
rows.hook: expanded the empire to its greatest size and is honored with a tall victory column

rows.label: Akhenaten
rows.hook: tried to switch his country to worship of a single sun disc god and moved the capital

rows.label: Gaius Marius
rows.description: Roman general, statesman and military reformer (157-86 BC)
rows.hook: was a seven-time consul who reformed the army and fought a civil war against a rival dictator

rows.label: Diocletian
rows.description: Augustus of the Eastern Roman Empire (244-311)
rows.hook: split the empire's rule among four men in the Tetrarchy and retired to grow cabbages

rows.label: Caracalla
rows.hook: is remembered for murdering his brother and granting citizenship to almost all free people in the empire

rows.label: Nefertiti
rows.description: Egyptian queen and Great Royal Wife (chief consort) of Akhenaten, an Egyptian Pharaoh
rows.hook: was a queen whose painted limestone bust is one of the most famous portraits from antiquity

rows.label: Domitian
rows.hook: was an emperor who finished the Colosseum's construction work but was assassinated after a paranoid reign

rows.label: Virgil
rows.hook: wrote the national epic following Aeneas, the Trojan refugee who founded a new homeland

rows.label: Pliny the Elder
rows.hook: wrote a giant encyclopedia of the natural world and died studying the eruption of Vesuvius

rows.label: Ovid
rows.hook: wrote the Metamorphoses, a long poem of mythological transformations, and was exiled by the emperor

rows.label: Elagabalus
rows.hook: was a teenage emperor who was a priest of a Syrian sun god and was killed by his own guard

rows.label: Septimius Severus
rows.hook: was an African-born emperor who won a civil war and died campaigning in Britain

rows.label: Titus
rows.hook: crushed the Jewish revolt in Jerusalem and opened the Colosseum, and ruled during the eruption of Vesuvius

rows.label: Aurelian
rows.hook: reunited the breakaway parts of the empire and built a great wall around the capital

rows.label: Vespasian
rows.description: ninth Roman Emperor and founder of the Flavian dynasty (69–79)
rows.hook: won the Year of the Four Emperors and began building the Colosseum

rows.label: Marcus Licinius Crassus
rows.hook: was the richest man in the city, teamed up with two rivals in a triumvirate, and died fighting the Parthians

rows.label: Tacitus
rows.hook: was a senator and historian who wrote the Annals and the Germania

rows.label: Marcus Junius Brutus
rows.hook: was the best-known conspirator who joined the plot to stab his friend and dictator, and later lost at Philippi

rows.label: Nerva
rows.hook: was an elderly senator who became emperor after a tyrant's assassination and ruled only briefly

rows.label: Plutarch
rows.description: Greek philosopher and historian (c. AD 46 – after AD 119)
rows.hook: wrote Parallel Lives, paired biographies of famous Greeks and their counterparts

rows.label: Ptolemy
rows.hook: wrote the Almagest and put the Earth at the center of the universe in a model used for centuries

rows.label: Hatshepsut
rows.description: 5th Pharaoh of the Eighteenth Dynasty of Egypt (c. 1479 BC - 1458 BC)
rows.hook: was a female pharaoh who ruled as king and built a grand terraced temple at Deir el-Bahari

rows.label: Scipio Africanus
rows.hook: defeated Hannibal at the Battle of Zama and ended the Second Punic War

rows.label: Josephus
rows.hook: was a Jewish rebel commander who switched sides and wrote a history of the Jewish War

rows.label: Epictetus
rows.hook: was a Stoic philosopher who had been a slave and taught that we control only our own judgments

rows.label: Theodosius I
rows.hook: was the last emperor to rule both halves of the empire and made Nicene Christianity the state faith

rows.label: Antoninus Pius
rows.hook: was a peaceful emperor who ruled during a golden age and adopted the philosopher who followed him

rows.label: Livia
rows.description: first Roman empress as consort to Augustus, as well as mother of emperor Tiberius
rows.hook: was the influential wife of the first emperor, rumored to have schemed to put her son on the throne

rows.label: Suetonius
rows.hook: wrote gossipy biographies called The Twelve Caesars

rows.label: Germanicus
rows.description: nephew and adopted son of emperor Tiberius, heir apparent of the Roman Empire, and father of emperor Caligula
rows.hook: was a beloved general and popular heir whose early death, possibly by poison, shocked the empire

rows.label: Martial
rows.hook: was a poet famous for sharp, witty epigrams, and gave the name to short satirical verse

rows.label: Galba
rows.hook: took the throne after a tyrant's suicide and was murdered by the guard after only months

rows.label: Vitellius
rows.hook: was a gluttonous emperor who held power for only months and was dragged through the streets to his death

rows.label: Narmer
rows.description: ancient Egyptian pharaoh of the Early Dynastic Period
rows.hook: is often credited with uniting the two lands into one kingdom, and appears on a famous ceremonial palette

rows.label: Agrippina the Younger
rows.description: Roman empress and member of the Julio-Claudian dynasty (AD 15–59)
rows.hook: was the mother of a notorious emperor, and her son later had her killed

rows.label: Khufu
rows.hook: ordered the construction of the Great Pyramid of Giza, the largest ever built

rows.label: Imhotep
rows.description: Egyptian architect, physician, astronomer, and god of medicine in ancient Egyptian mythology.
rows.hook: was a royal architect credited with designing the first step pyramid, later worshiped as a god of healing

rows.label: Cato the Younger
rows.description: Roman statesman, general and writer (95–46 BC)
rows.hook: was a stubborn defender of the old republic who took his own life rather than submit to a dictator

rows.label: Otho
rows.hook: was one of four emperors in a single turbulent year, and took his own life after a lost battle

rows.label: Seti I
rows.description: second pharaoh of Ancient Egypt's 19th dynasty
rows.hook: built a magnificent tomb in the Valley of the Kings and a temple at Abydos, and fathered a famous builder-king

rows.label: Horace
rows.hook: wrote the Odes and coined the phrase carpe diem

rows.label: Thutmose III
rows.description: sixth Egyptian Pharaoh of the Eighteenth Dynasty
rows.hook: was a warrior-pharaoh who led many campaigns and is sometimes called the Napoleon of his land

rows.label: Galen
rows.hook: served as doctor to gladiators and emperors and shaped medical thinking for over a thousand years

rows.label: Messalina
rows.hook: was the wife of Emperor Claudius, remembered for a scandalous reputation and a dramatic downfall

rows.label: Severus Alexander
rows.hook: was a young emperor killed by his own mutinous troops, ending a dynasty

rows.label: Lucius Verus
rows.description: joint Roman Emperor with Marcus Aurelius (161–169)
rows.hook: shared the throne with the philosopher-emperor who wrote Meditations

rows.label: Amenhotep III
rows.description: ninth Pharaoh of the Eighteenth dynasty of Egypt
rows.hook: was a wealthy pharaoh, father of the heretic king Akhenaten and grandfather of Tutankhamun

rows.label: Philip the Arab
rows.hook: was an emperor from the Syrian desert who hosted the thousandth birthday of the empire's capital

rows.label: Lucius Tarquinius Superbus
rows.description: king of Rome from 535 to 509 BC
rows.hook: was the last king, whose overthrow led to the founding of the Republic

rows.label: Pliny the Younger
rows.description: Roman lawyer, author and magistrate (61 – c.113)
rows.hook: wrote eyewitness letters describing the eruption of Vesuvius that buried Pompeii

rows.label: Titus Livius
rows.hook: wrote a giant history of the city from its legendary founding onward

rows.label: Cato the Elder
rows.description: Roman politician, soldier and writer (234–149 BC)
rows.hook: ended his speeches by demanding that Carthage must be destroyed

rows.label: Constantius II
rows.hook: was a son of Constantine the Great who ruled after his father's death

rows.label: Valentinian I
rows.hook: was a soldier-emperor who divided the empire with his brother Valens

rows.label: Nefertari
rows.hook: was the beloved queen of Ramesses the Great, honored with a spectacular painted tomb

rows.label: Plotinus
rows.description: Hellenistic Platonist philosopher and founder of Neoplatonism (c. 204/5–270)
rows.hook: taught that all reality flows from a single ultimate source he called the One

rows.label: Ramesses I
rows.description: founding pharaoh of Ancient Egypt's Nineteenth Dynasty
rows.hook: was an army officer who became pharaoh and founded a dynasty, but ruled for barely more than a year

rows.label: Ramesses III
rows.hook: won major battles against the mysterious Sea Peoples and is often called the last great New Kingdom pharaoh

rows.label: Vitruvius
rows.hook: wrote the only complete architecture treatise to survive from antiquity

rows.label: Gallienus
rows.hook: reigned during the Crisis of the Third Century as the empire nearly fell apart

rows.label: Catullus
rows.description: lyric Latin poet of the Roman Republic
rows.hook: wrote passionate love poems to a woman he called Lesbia
